## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

content.thinking: The user is asking about the rocket's smoke rendering logic - specifically where the count/number of smoke particles is determined. Let me look at the Rocket.ts file since that's where the rocket logic would be.

content.text: 로켓 스모크 파티클 개수 결정 로직을 찾아볼게요.

input.description: Find rocket smoke particle count logic
input.prompt:
In resource/ts/objects/rocket/Rocket.ts and any related smoke/particle files, find where the smoke particle COUNT is determined. Look for:
- How many smoke instances/particles are created
- Any config values controlling smoke count
- Constructor params or config objects that set particle numbers
- Any related smoke classes/files imported into Rocket.ts

Report the exact file paths and line numbers for where the count is set. Keep it concise.

content.text:
That is everything needed. Here is the complete picture:

---

**There are no "smoke particles" in `Rocket.ts` itself.** The rocket's smoke is handled entirely by the `GravityBalls` class. The particle count is determined in two places:

**1. Config value — spawned per update tick**

`c:\Users\edn_y\renew_nineonelabs\resource\ts\config\object.config.ts`, line 446:
```ts
dotsPerInterval: 15,
```
This is the value passed from the scene config into `GravityBalls`. It controls how many smoke sprites are spawned on every update call.

**2. Fallback default inside `GravityBalls`**

`c:\Users\edn_y\renew_nineonelabs\resource\ts\objects\main\GravityBalls.ts`, line 45:
```ts
dotsPerInterval: 3,
```
This is the internal `DEFAULTS.dotsPerInterval` used when no config value is provided.

**3. Spawn site (the actual loop)**

`c:\Users\edn_y\renew_nineonelabs\resource\ts\objects\main\GravityBalls.ts`, line 119:
```ts
for (let i = 0; i < o.dotsPerInterval; i++) this._spawn(ctx, o);
```
This is where the count drives actual particle creation each frame tick. There is no fixed pool or cap — particles live for `LIFETIME_TICKS = 150` ticks (line 34) before being removed, so the steady-state count is approximately `dotsPerInterval × 150` alive simultaneously (15 × 150 = ~2250 at the configured value).

**No smoke classes are imported into `Rocket.ts`** — the two objects are independent `SceneObject` instances configured separately in `object.config.ts`.

# Frontend Rules

- Bundler: Vite / Language: TypeScript (ES6+)
- 3D: Three.js. Main scenes use `core/Engine.ts`; works scatter is the standalone secondary renderer in `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`.
- **Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`**
  - Reason: Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-bundles on every file save
  - Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency
  - Do not include these commands in verification steps, PR notes, or agent plans

## TypeScript

- All shared types/interfaces/enums live in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`; avoid inline exported types and `any`.
- Shared constants, colors, sizes, URLs, selectors, and timings live in `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts` or page scene config files.
- Page theatre: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Page scene/config composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Page-only lifecycle/runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`
- Standalone page renderer exception: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/render/` (currently works scatter)
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.

## Three.js

- `dispose()` required for every geometry, material, texture, render target, and standalone renderer.
- Main WebGL renderer ownership belongs to `Engine`; standalone secondary renderers must call `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- No object creation inside render loops or RAF hot paths.
- `addEventListener` must have matching `removeEventListener`.
- No monkey-patching Three.js API.

# Frontend Rules

- Bundler: Vite / Language: TypeScript (ES6+)
- 3D: Three.js. Main scenes use `core/Engine.ts`; works scatter is the standalone secondary renderer in `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`.
- **Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`**
  - Reason: Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-bundles on every file save
  - Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency
  - Do not include these commands in verification steps, PR notes, or agent plans

## TypeScript

- All shared types/interfaces/enums live in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`; avoid inline exported types and `any`.
- Shared constants, colors, sizes, URLs, selectors, and timings live in `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts` or page scene config files.
- Page theatre: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Page scene/config composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Page-only lifecycle/runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`
- Standalone page renderer exception: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/render/` (currently works scatter)
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.

## Three.js

- `dispose()` required for every geometry, material, texture, render target, and standalone renderer.
- Main WebGL renderer ownership belongs to `Engine`; standalone secondary renderers must call `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- No object creation inside render loops or RAF hot paths.
- `addEventListener` must have matching `removeEventListener`.
- No monkey-patching Three.js API.
